items.title: GL.iNet Owners Find a Second Backdoor on Their Routers, Some Planted in 2025
items.summary: Owners checking their GL.iNet routers for Friday’s cloud attack have found a separate, older backdoor, on some routers since the autumn of 2025. It isn’t in GL.iNet’s security notice of 20 November, and the check GL.iNet tells owners to run doesn’t find it. It starts with the router, reports to servers named to look like AdGuard and OpenWrt, and survives firmware updates that keep the settings. The scale is not small. items.title: Revealed: profiles of UK experts on gambling harm being hijacked to push illegal online casinos
items.summary: Findings highlight unscrupulous tactics used by operators in multibillion pound illicit market and challenges facing authorities Prof Heather Wardle has dedicated 20 years to researching the harm caused by gambling. items.title: Hackers Could Execute Commands on WordPress, Email and Print Servers Through Upload2Shell Flaw
items.summary: A flaw in Ghostscript let researchers run commands on WordPress, Roundcube webmail, and Linux print servers through routine file processing. The vulnerability, dubbed Upload2Shell and tracked as CVE-2026-125396, affects upstream Ghostscript releases before 10.08.0. It sits in the software’s Type 1 font loader, but the affected servers did not need to expose Ghostscript directly. Their own preview, thumbnail, and print features delivered files to it. items.title: Cairn AI Framework Used in Autonomous Zero-Day Exploitation
items.summary: Amazon uncovered AI-powered attacks on universities, where autonomous agents found a zero-day and gained root access without human guidance. Amazon’s threat intelligence team found a Chinese-nexus actor running Cairn, an open-source AI pentesting framework, with one instruction for the agents: obtain shell access. No human chose the next step after that. The agents planned, executed, and adjusted on their own, and along the way they found a real zero-day in an open-source medical imaging application.
